sources.title: Daly and colleagues: Archaeological evidence of the late fourteenth-century tsunami
sources.note: Original PNAS 2019 DOI10.1073/pnas.1902241116 full indexed text checked; direct open later showed CAPTCHA. Results ceramic clusters and Methods surface survey, not excavated houses. Speculative tsunami-to-state causal narrative not treated as established.

sources.note: Direct original scholarly PDF. Printed38 to 40 royal trade control,1629 naval defeat,1632 concessions;35 to 36 later Asian networks and tin.

sources.title: National Archives of Indonesia: Aceh in 1689, introduction by Sher Banu Khan
sources.note: Direct institutional scholarly introduction:1641 to 1699 four queens;1663/1668 treaties and company pressure. Combined conservatively with same dossier primary translation in work-level check.

sources.title: National Archives of Indonesia: The Eagle’s 1689 memorandum, English translation
sources.note: Direct archival primary source, Batavia Castle journal2November1689,fols807 to 818. Foreign traders’ observations, not a census; ignore sexist queen-only-in-name claim, contested by scholarship. Houses fol807,food/textiles fol811,seasonal shopping fol817 to 818.

sources.title: Ma. Theresa R. Milallos: Women and Islam in pre-nineteenth-century Aceh
sources.note: Direct National Library Board research essay. Money changers/slavery paragraphs155 to 159; late nineteenth-century inheritance/juree paragraphs124 to 126. Do not adopt erroneous early-fifteenth-century unification chronology or universal female autonomy.

sources.title: National Library Board: Revisiting the Mystery of the Missing Gold Coins
sources.note: Direct2023research article, Acehnese Gold Coins section: mas/debasement/merchant reluctance. Do not use reconstructed Jawi tables from missing coins as surviving script witness.

sources.title: Raja Iskandar Bin Raja Halid: The Adat Aceh, a seventeenth-century Malay soundscape
sources.note: Author-uploaded original complete2021article,DOI10.1080/13639811.2021.1959144. Printed396 visiting scholars;397 to 398 Adat transmission, Ramadan instruments. Later copies explicitly distinguished from ceremonies described.
